content.text: A typo in a config change (50 to 5 connections) directly caused checkout requests to queue and timeout. This highlights a critical vulnerability in the deployment process for configuration changes.

ai.stableNodeKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#0

content.text: The error-rate alert fired 22 minutes after the config change, due to a 15-minute threshold. This delay meant customers experienced errors for a significant period before the incident was formally detected.

ai.stableNodeKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#1

content.text: Once the alert fired, rollback and full recovery took 25 minutes. The total customer impact was 47 minutes, with 2,300 failed checkouts.

ai.stableNodeKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#2

content.text: The review identified three key process gaps: slow alert thresholds, delayed status page updates, and a lack of review for config changes.

ai.stableNodeKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#3

content.text: Actions agreed upon include lowering the checkout error-rate alert to 5% over 5 minutes, allowing support to directly update the status page, and implementing pull-request review for payments service config changes.

ai.stableNodeKey: Post-incident review: checkout outage, March 14 § text#4

content.text: Decisions on a Friday deploy freeze and automatic rollback are deferred, pending further analysis. The status of customer retries for failed checkouts is also an open question.
